item.title: Version 1.10.0
item.description:
Version 1.10.0

  • Contact: the developer's website (ilan.solutions) is now linked on the activation screen, in About, Settings and Help, and from Help → Developer Website.

Version 1.9.0

  • Contact: the developer's email address (dev@ilan.solutions) is now on the activation screen, in License messages, About, Settings and Help, with Email the Developer… in the Help menu and the menu bar icon.

Version 1.8.1

  • License check: Mac Checkup no longer downloads the old public list of deactivated keys from GitHub. It only asks the developer's private license service about this Mac's own key.

Version 1.7.0

  • License check: deactivated keys are now checked privately. Once a day Mac Checkup asks the developer's license service about this Mac's key only, sending a one-way code made from its ID, instead of downloading a public list. Nothing else is sent, and the service keeps no record of who asked.
  • A key that the developer restores starts working again by itself at the next daily check, without entering it again.

Version 1.6.0

  • New Home page: Mac Checkup opens with four tiles (Internet, Wi-Fi, This Mac, Security), one-click buttons for common problems, your latest connection drop and the most important things to look at.
  • Easier to find things: the sidebar groups the tools by job (Wi-Fi tools, Connection, Apps & sites, Advanced) with a short plain-English line under each, and the groups open and close. Search (⌘K) finds pages, findings and Help topics, even from a symptom like "zoom choppy".
  • Answer first on every page: under the title, the most important finding (or "No problems found") and when the page was last checked. ⌘R or Check Again runs it again; the ? next to the title opens that page's Help.
  • Keyboard shortcuts: ⌘1 to ⌘9 jump to the main pages (new Go menu).
  • First-launch setup: three steps on Home (run a Full Checkup, turn on Connection Monitor, enter your plan speed). Hide them any time; Help → Show Setup Steps brings them back.
  • Menu bar: new Run Speed Test, What's Wrong? and Snapshot Now.

Version 1.5.0

  • Connection Monitor: every drop now shows where it broke — Wi-Fi, your router, the modem/line to your provider, your provider's network, or the VPN — from a snapshot taken the moment it happened. The outage report, CSV log and support bundle include it, and Snapshot Now checks on demand.
  • Website Check: new Work apps list (Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace — editable) checked in one click, with lookup/connect/handshake/server timings and an "it's me or them" verdict. Redirected sites now show their full timing breakdown.
  • Path & NAT and Full Checkup: asks your router for its own internet address (UPnP/NAT-PMP, read-only) to detect double NAT and carrier-grade NAT reliably, even through a VPN, and shows your NAT type (Open, Moderate, Strict).
  • New Bandwidth by App page: live upload and download per app on this Mac, with plain names for macOS services and a warning when a big upload or download will make calls choppy.
  • Bufferbloat: results are now saved and charted over time, and the latest grade appears on Speed Test.
  • DNS & VPN: new HTTPS inspection check (is something decrypting your secure traffic?) and Blocked ports check (web, email, VPN, remote desktop and video-call ports).
  • Wi-Fi Walk Test: new floor plan heatmap — add a picture of your floor plan, click where each reading was taken, and see weak spots in colour.

Version 1.4.0

  • Fix buttons on findings: problems a Quick Fix can solve now have a Fix: … button right on the finding, on any page. After the fix, Mac Checkup checks again and shows whether it worked.
  • What's Wrong? re-checks after a fix: it runs the same diagnosis again and tells you Fixed, Better, or Still there.
  • Call Quality: new 60-second test (like a real call) and a Ready / Borderline / Not ready verdict for Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet and FaceTime.

  • Share Report: new support bundle — one .zip with the PDF, connection log, speed history, walk tests, checkup history and a network settings snapshot (packet capture optional).

  • LAN Devices: shows what each device is and who made it (from Bonjour), finds devices that ignore ping, flags New devices you haven't seen before, and adds a fix button for IP conflicts.

  • Connection Monitor: new Last 7 days summary (drops, time offline, Wi-Fi disconnects, typical speed) and an optional weekly summary notification.
  • Share Report: new support bundle — one .zip with the PDF, connection log, speed history, walk tests, checkup history and a network settings snapshot (packet capture optional).

Version 1.3.1

  • Fixed: Packet Capture didn't stop when the countdown reached 0 and kept recording in the background (until 200,000 packets). It now stops on time, then shows "Finishing the recording…" while it saves and analyses.

Version 1.3.0

  • New What's Wrong? page: pick a symptom (Wi-Fi keeps dropping, video calls are choppy, a website won't load, internet is slow, my Mac is slow) and get one plain answer with the cause and next steps — a Quick Fix, the right page, or a report for your provider.
  • New Wi-Fi Walk Test: measure signal, Wi-Fi link speed and latency room by room, see weak spots on a chart, and get advice on where a mesh node would help.
  • New Speed vs Plan: enter your plan speed, log every speed test (optionally on a schedule), see how much of the plan you really get, the slowest time of day and outages, and create an Internet Service Report PDF for your provider.
  • New Bufferbloat test: grades A+ to F how much delay your connection adds when busy (downloading and uploading), with router settings to fix it.
  • New Website Check: is it down for everyone or just you? Compares your DNS with Cloudflare and Google, spots sites blocked by filters like Pi-hole (even through redirects), and times each step of loading the site.

  • License keys: Mac Checkup is activated with a license key from the developer. Settings → License shows who it's licensed to; the name also appears in About and on PDF reports.

Version 1.1.0

  • Fixed: the menu bar icon could freeze on an old status (often a false "offline" or "slow") for up to half an hour. macOS App Nap was pausing the app while it sat in the menu bar; it now keeps checking on schedule (your Mac still sleeps normally), and checks interrupted by a pause are ignored instead of reported.
  • Travelling / not connected: no network (Wi-Fi off, out of range, on a plane) is logged as information, not as a drop; it doesn't send alerts or lower uptime. New menu bar badge (–) for it.
  • Hotel, airport and café Wi-Fi: detects when the network needs you to sign in on a web page, shows a key badge in the menu bar and sends one notification.
  • New Packet Capture tool: records traffic for 15 s to 2 min and explains the results in plain English (failed DNS lookups, unanswered or refused connections, signs of packet loss, top hosts, kinds of traffic). Save, delete or open the capture in Wireshark.
  • New installer window: the DMG opens to "Install Mac Checkup" with an arrow showing where to drag the app.
